parsed.explanation: Combined regime: state law is among the most protective—no mapped facility ban, public-accommodations/employment/housing nondiscrimination, gender-identity hate-crime coverage, X markers without medical proof, and a care shield law—so everyday interior exposure is low. That does not cancel the federal layer every visitor meets: binary sex definition, federal-facility exclusion, stopped X/mismatched passport processing, and entry-screening instructions to refuse on document discrepancy and consider permanent fraud ineligibility for suspected misrepresentation. Federal custody abuses documented nationally—forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse in immigration custody, and conversion-therapy practices in corrections—raise severity if detained. Litigation has blocked some orders, leaving uncertainty, not safety.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary-sex passport policy, X/mismatch processing stopped, entry cable directs refusal on discrepancy/doubt and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility for suspected wilful misrepresentation. Status documented.
entry_documents.protection: State X option on licences/birth certificates and marker change without surgery; existing X passports valid until expiry. Does not override federal entry screening.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor's home documents meet federal screening first; state marker rules do not preempt refusal or fraud consideration at entry.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections conversion-therapy model and immigration-custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse of trans men. Status documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No visitor-specific custody protocol or remedy documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry discrepancy or facility arrest can move visitor into federal/state custody where documented abuse severity is high.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; many states ban facilities, 4 make it criminal in circumstances, with a trespass arrest documented nationally.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state is not among mapped school/government-building ban states and prohibits discrimination in public accommodations since 2006.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State facilities are protected locally; federal buildings, airports and federally funded facilities remain under federal exclusion—both apply in one journey.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders target minor gender-affirming care and funding; youth-care bans in 27 states nationally create home-state restrictions.
care_services.protection: State shield law protects patients/providers from civil/criminal charges for care lawful here but banned at home; insurance nondiscrimination and mandated reassignment coverage. Invocation details not documented.
care_services.interaction: Shield may help a travelling minor/parent obtain lawful care locally, but does not cancel federal funding, investigation, or entry consequences.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal executive orders, sports and school investigations, counterterrorism language including 'radically pro-transgender' groups, and 66% poll support for assigned-sex documents signal official/social hostility.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State hate-crime statute covers gender identity/expression; panic defences abolished; state nondiscrimination laws in housing, employment, public accommodations, insurance.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State protections operate locally; federal threat-framing and enforcement priorities shape border, federal facility and custody encounters.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal January 2025 order directs investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; student bathroom arrests and school bans documented nationally.
minors_guardians.protection: State anti-bullying and education-equity laws cover gender identity; conversion therapy on minors banned since 2018; shield law relevant to care-seeking families.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor is protected in state schools/care locally, but federal school/care orders and entry screening follow the family and create uncertainty where orders are enjoined.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific anti-trans violence, hate-crime prosecution or police-response figures documented; national bathroom arrest involved handcuffing and 24h men's-ward hold.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime coverage and nondiscrimination machinery are documented, with no documented enforcement intensity.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of local violence data is not safety; federal/state police arrest power shown in restroom enforcement interacts with local protections.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport and executive-order challenges unresolved; several orders blocked/enjoined; remedies for refused entry are slow and uncertain in practice.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation, courts allowing challenges, state commission and legal-aid FAQ documented; no documented visitor remedy that overrides federal screening.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation may change federal rules mid-travel; state remedies do not guarantee release from federal refusal, detention or facility exclusion.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: extended screening on document discrepancy, discretionary refusal/return rather than routine imprisonment, slow rarely revised remedies. Higher than this anchor for interior life due to state protections and no state facility ban; lower in fraud-eligibility severity.

Similar in that frontline document questioning occurs despite formal protections and an advocate may help, with delay/cost but no certain detention. Lower here because federal cable contemplates permanent ineligibility and custody abuse is documented, unlike the anchor's barred detention.

Lower than this anchor: that case has respectful entry, trained officers, counsel and compensation for unlawful holding. Here federal screening, facility exclusion and custody harms are operative, even though the state tier is protective.

Materially lower: that anchor recognises trans/nonbinary passports, bodies cameras, legal aid and tribunal release. Here X processing is stopped federally, entry refusal/fraud consideration is instructed, and federal facilities exclude congruent access.

parsed.synthesis: The operative interaction is federal-first, state-protective second. At entry and in federal facilities/custody the traveller faces documented refusal, fraud-eligibility scrutiny, exclusion and severe custody risk; inside state-regulated hotels, clinics, schools and public accommodations the Most Protective tier, shield law and nondiscrimination/hate-crime laws reduce everyday exposure. State law does not preempt federal screening or custody, so the combined score sits in elevated risk, above a uniformly hostile regime but below purely protective anchors.
